verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Hot JOLTS + Suspended Iran Talks Keep the Framework Stuck; AI the Only Bid
verdict.rationale_short: The morning STEP ASIDE call held. JOLTS printed a hot 7.6M April openings (vs ~7.2M consensus), keeping the 30Y pinned near 5.00% for a fourth session without a clean sub-5.0% close. Indices drifted lower from Monday's record — S&P 500 ~-0.14% (~7,589), Nasdaq ~-0.25% (~27,019), Dow ~-0.09%, Russell 2000 ~-0.47% — with breadth narrowing to a handful of AI names: NVDA pushed toward $232 on Vera Rubin entering full production at COMPUTEX, while GOOGL stayed stopped out below $378 and META/AAPL lagged. Iran talks remain suspended with the Hormuz-closure threat live and Brent near $95. None of the two upgrade conditions (Iran de-escalation AND 30Y Day-2 sub-5.0%) is met. Stay stepped aside: hold NVDA (stop $215, no add), hold the ≤25% XLE stub (cover above $97), no new broad-index or rate-sensitive longs until the June 5 payrolls and Iran resolve.

bear_case: Two down sessions off the record are mild, but the composition keeps deteriorating. The market spent May pricing AI capex, rate relief, and an Iran deal; within 48 hours of the June 1 record the rate leg was undercut by a hot JOLTS (7.6M openings holding the 30Y at ~5.00%) and the deal leg was replaced by a suspended negotiation and a threat to close the Strait of Hormuz entirely. A Hormuz closure is a structural inflation shock that would push Warsh's committee toward the hike prediction markets already give >60% odds by December. The index is leaning on a shrinking set of leaders — NVDA near $232 while GOOGL is stopped out, META is down on EU DSA findings, AAPL lags, and the Russell underperforms for a seventh session — the narrow-breadth profile that precedes sharper drawdowns when the leaders finally wobble. Friday's May payrolls are the decisive test: a hot print on top of today's hot JOLTS makes the June 17 FOMC a live hike. Invalidation: Iran talks formally resume AND the 30Y closes below 5.00% for two consecutive sessions returns the framework to HOLD; conversely, Brent above $97 with the 30Y above 5.05%, or an SPX close below 7,460, converts STEP ASIDE to bearish — exit all longs.
